alerts.title: Missing TDF Renal Monitoring
alerts.message: Guidelines require creatinine (eGFR) monitoring for TDF at 3 months, 6 months, and then 6-12 monthly, especially in high-risk patients with hypertension. The patient has hypertension and is on TDF. The clinician's plan does not include scheduling the next required creatinine/eGFR test. While the current creatinine of 112 umol/L is within normal limits, the absence of a scheduled follow-up test is a monitoring gap.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule the next creatinine (eGFR) test as per the 6-12 monthly monitoring guideline for TDF.

alerts.title: Suboptimal BP Control
alerts.message: The patient's blood pressure is 146/94 mmHg, indicating suboptimal control. He admits to missing doses of amlodipine. Poorly controlled hypertension increases cardiovascular risk and can contribute to renal damage, which is a concern for a patient on TDF. The clinician's plan to refill amlodipine and encourage adherence is appropriate but may be insufficient.

evidence.recommended_action: Reinforce antihypertensive adherence and consider if dose adjustment or additional agent is needed per hypertension guidelines.

alerts.title: Trace Proteinuria Needs Evaluation
alerts.message: Trace proteinuria was noted. While attributed to hypertension, TDF is also associated with renal tubular damage and proteinuria. The patient has two potential causes: hypertension and long-term TDF use. The plan does not include further evaluation of proteinuria (e.g., urine protein-to-creatinine ratio) to determine the cause and severity.

evidence.recommended_action: Evaluate trace proteinuria further with a urine protein-to-creatinine ratio to guide management.
